exposure: Patient demographics (age, gender, preferred language, zip code of residence, primary insurance plan)
cohort: The study included 1,495 telemedicine visits in 2020 and 1,983 in-person visits in 2019 for nonurgent pediatric otolaryngology services.
finding: There were no significant differences in patient age, gender, Spanish-speaking families, Medi-Cal-insured patients, or mean poverty level between telemedicine visits in 2020 and in-person visits in 2019, but Spanish-speaking families were statistically more likely to require rescheduling of their telemedicine visits.
